title: Retry and time out a protocol step
description: A transient step failure today costs a whole performance: the only recovery is diagnosis leading to reperform or recast, which was designed for structural failure rather than a flaky call. ProtocolStep has no retry and no timeout. Add both plus StageOptions defaults, and make every attempt visible in the trace so flakiness cannot hide behind a green run. A timeout turns a hanging step into a failed turn, which needs the abort signal -- hence the blocker.
acceptance_criteria: ProtocolStep.retry (attempts, backoff) and timeoutMs with stage-level defaults; each attempt records a trace event; a timed-out step yields a failed turn rather than a hang; optional and owns semantics preserved; R-STEP requirements and docs.

title: Pass an AbortSignal through a performance
description: drama has no cancellation: nothing in src/ mentions signal or abort. Every engine in the survey supports it, and it is a prerequisite for a step timeout that does not lie -- you cannot stop an in-flight model call, only abandon waiting for it. Smallest reversible design: StageOptions.signal, checked between waves, and the same signal exposed on ActorContext so an executor can abort its own transport call.
acceptance_criteria: StageOptions.signal stops a running performance between waves; executors receive it through ActorContext; an aborted performance ends in a distinct inspectable outcome rather than a throw; R-ABORT requirements and docs.
notes: Implemented in debe4a0. StageOptions.signal + ActorContext.signal; a new PerformanceStatus 'aborted' on the result and the finished event; canceled performances skip evaluation. R-ABORT-1..6 in test/requirements/abort.requirements.test.ts; full suite 206 pass / 0 fail, typecheck exit 0. Deliberate limit documented: the check is between waves, so casting/auditioning already ran.

title: Make a gated performance resumable
description: Approver is an in-process predicate (GateRequest) => boolean | Promise<boolean> and fails closed, so a gate with no human present simply halts the show. Durable suspend and resume is the one genuine advantage the surveyed engines have. drama is unusually well placed for it: the trace and the cast are data, and only executors are re-attached, as R-SERIAL-6 proves. Smallest reversible design to start from: pause at gate boundaries rather than after every turn, persist, and resume later with the approval.
acceptance_criteria: a gated performance can pause, persist, and resume to completion with the approval supplied afterwards; the paused state reuses the existing serialization; fail-closed behaviour is preserved when no approval ever arrives; requirements and docs.

title: Optional content contract for artifacts (structured output)
description: expectedOutput names artifact kinds, but the content is unguarded: the total-normalizer discipline stops at the card boundary. All five engines now support native structured output (Mastra structuredOutput, OpenAI response_format, Anthropic output_config.format with a JSON schema). Add an optional per-kind contract so createLlmExecutor can request and validate it. Zero-dependency constraint: accept a host-provided validator or a minimal subset. A validation failure must be a failed turn rather than a throw, so that it composes with retry.
acceptance_criteria: an actor can declare an artifact content contract; the LLM path validates it; a mismatch fails the turn with the validation error visible; no new runtime dependencies; requirements and docs.

title: Carry executor usage and support a cost budget
description: maxTurns counts executions, which is a poor proxy for cost: one turn with a large context can cost orders of magnitude more than another. The words usage and cost appear nowhere in src/. Engines expose usage in their responses, so passing it through is free. Side effect worth having: it also unblocks the WISE judge-panel stop rule (arXiv:2608.19802), which was declined in docs/graph-engineering.md precisely because drama had no cost data.
acceptance_criteria: ActorOutput.usage flows into ActorTurn and the trace without breaking serialization; StageOptions.maxCostUsd halts a performance like the other budgets; requirements and docs updated.

title: Borrow the missing agent-engine primitives
description: Close the gaps found comparing drama against the top-5 agent engines (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, Google ADK, CrewAI, Mastra), recorded in docs/prior-art.md. Every item is a primitive those engines treat as table stakes and drama lacks; nothing here is engine parity for its own sake, and the explicit non-goals (streaming, memory/RAG, MCP client, per-actor model routing, deployment) stay non-goals.
acceptance_criteria: Each child issue is implemented with R-id requirements per docs/requirements.md convention, the suite and typecheck are green, and docs are updated where behaviour is documented.

title: Export a performance trace as OpenTelemetry-shaped spans
description: ActorTurn already carries per-turn timings, status and actor identity, and performanceTimeline is essentially a span list, so this is an adapter rather than a core change. Emit OTLP-shaped JSON with zero dependencies and let the host export it. The structural fingerprint of R-DET-1 excludes timestamps, so determinism is unaffected.
acceptance_criteria: a function mapping a Performance to OTel-shaped spans; no new dependencies; deterministic for the same performance; requirements and docs.
